inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted average, H1 FY27 interim (26 weeks to 26 Sep 2026). Held flat: SBC (c.GBP 3m) is expensed in the flows and there have been no buybacks.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 Annual Report, share-based payment expense (BME.L_Annual_FY2026.txt:8791). No separate equity-award tax outflow is disclosed.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in GBP millions; LSE quote in pence (GBp). Model-to-quote conversion is the fixed 100 pence per pound, not a market FX rate, so it cannot go stale. Magnitude check: FY26 adjusted pre-IFRS 16 diluted EPS of 22.4p against the quote gives a P/E in the mid-teens, confirming the price is pence.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-18T15:35:52Z, last print of the 18 Nov regular LSE session (Yahoo Finance chart API)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in GBP. Assumed 10-year gilt c.4.5% + 5.0% UK equity risk premium x beta c.1.0 = c.9.5% cost of equity; after-tax cost of debt c.4.9% (6.5% coupon on the Nov 2024 bond x (1 - 25%)); debt c.15% of capital on the pre-IFRS 16 basis used here (leases are an operating cost in the flows, so they are not in the capital structure). Blended c.8.8%, rounded up to 9.0%. One WACC for all three scenarios: turnaround and competitive risk is carried in the scenario flows and weights, not in the discount rate. Reviewed after the sanity-check trip and left at 9.0%: the script's 'regulatory single point of failure' diagnosis is a keyword false positive for a general-merchandise retailer, none of the documented structural premiums (customer concentration, sub-$300m illiquidity, single-region, regulatory) applies to a c.GBP 3.7bn FTSE 250 company, and turnaround risk is already charged through the 25% bear weight; adding a premium would charge it twice.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. The EBITDA margin path is the company's adjusted EBITDA on the pre-IFRS 16 basis, which is already after the full store and warehouse rent charge (FY26 cash lease cost: GBP 192m principal + GBP 84m interest, both in financing activities). lease_cost_pct_path is therefore 0 to avoid charging rent twice, D&A is the pre-IFRS 16 figure (ex right-of-use depreciation), and net debt is the company's pre-IFRS 16 net debt of GBP 613m, excluding GBP 1,454m of lease liabilities.
inputs.nci_treatment: None. No non-controlling interest; the small Centz (Ireland) associate is ignored.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (operating retailer; dcf-methods routing row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical'), with the non-US adaptations: GBP-built WACC, GBp quote, lease treatment (B), near-zero SBC. First valuation 2026-11-19; revised the same day after the multiples sanity check tripped (bear terminal value capped at the historical-minimum EV/EBITDA; see valuation_philosophy and reconciliation). BASE-YEAR FCF: neither the FY26 trough nor a completed turnaround is extrapolated. FY26 reported FCF in the Metrics CSV (OCF 736 - capex 142 = 594) is before GBP 276m of lease cash paid through financing and includes roughly GBP 96m of working-capital inflow; reported_fcf here is the lease-adjusted figure (594 - 192 - 84 = 318) so that last_fcf = reported_fcf - SBC = 315. That 315 is still flattered by working capital and by a low GBP 65m cash tax bill on depressed profit; the component build gives a year-1 (FY27) unlevered owner FCF of roughly GBP 220m, and that component figure, not 315, is what the valuation rests on. Year 1 is anchored on the midpoint of FY27 guidance (adjusted pre-IFRS 16 EBITDA GBP 450-500m), less an allowance for recurring 'adjusting' items; the base case then recovers a little under half of the margin lost between FY23-25 (11.1-11.5%) and FY26 (7.9%). TIMING: FY0 is FY26 but net debt is the 26 Sep 2026 half-year figure, so H1 FY27 cash generation is in both net debt and the year-1 flow; against that, year 1 is discounted a full period although only about four months of FY27 remain, which pushes every later flow out by about 0.6 of a year. The second effect is the larger, so the net bias is modestly conservative. September net debt is also seasonally high (pre-Golden-Quarter stock build). The price is cum the 3.6p interim dividend, which goes ex on 19 Nov 2026. The price rose about 30% in the fortnight to 18 Nov on the H1 FY27 results and new guidance and sits at the top of its 52-week range (140.0-364.8). Interest income (GBP 6m) is received in investing activities and the company is in net debt, so nothing is stripped. Buybacks: none to date; the flat share count is a modelling convention costing GBP 3m a year.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (1.7-3.5%) diverges by far more than 30% from the EPS CAGR (-17% to -22%). Book equity is not a usable growth anchor here: B&M has paid out most of its earnings in ordinary and special dividends, so equity is roughly flat by policy, while EPS has fallen on margin compression rather than on lost sales. Revenue CAGR is used instead.
historical_growth.notes: FY2021-FY2026 annual rows; FY21 was the pandemic peak, which depresses every 5-year figure. FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (OCF - capex - lease principal - lease interest - SBC): FY21 c.535, FY23 453, FY24 377, FY25 286, FY26 315. Statutory FCF as stored in the CSV (before lease cash) fell more slowly, 739 to 594, because rising lease payments sit in financing.

base.ebitda_margin_note: Company adjusted EBITDA margin, pre-IFRS 16 (after rent), less c.0.1-0.2pp for recurring adjusting items. History: FY23 11.5%, FY24 11.5%, FY25 11.1%, FY26 7.9%. Year 1 = FY27 guidance midpoint GBP 475m on c.GBP 5,980m revenue (7.95%) less c.GBP 10m of adjusting items. Mature 9.5% recovers about 45% of the FY26 margin loss; the statutory cost step-up (minimum wage, employer NI, EPR levy) is treated as permanent.
base.growth_note: H1 FY27 revenue +3.6%. FY28 onward: UK openings revert to 25-35 gross, France 15-20 a year, low-single-digit LFL; fading to 2.5% as the UK estate matures.
base.capex_note: FY24-FY26 actual 2.3-2.5% of revenue, about 1% of it maintenance. FY28 carries the refit/re-lay programme. Capex is held above D&A in the terminal year because the terminal still grows.
base.wc_note: Negative: net operating working capital (inventory + receivables - payables) was GBP 247m at March 2026, 4.3% of revenue, so growth consumes cash.
base.tax_note: UK and French statutory rate 25%; adjusted effective rate was 24% in FY26 and 25% in H1 FY27. FY26 cash tax of GBP 65m reflected depressed profit and is not carried forward.
base.terminal_cap_note: Exit-multiple cap tested and not binding. On the like-for-like IFRS 16 basis the Gordon terminal value is 7.1x EBITDA against a 10-year average of 7.59x; the existing 15x FCF cap is tighter than the historical-multiple cap (15.8x FCF equivalent) and is kept.

bull.ebitda_margin_note: Year 1 near the top of FY27 guidance (c.GBP 490m). Mature 11.0% group margin corresponds to management's stated medium-term ambition of a low-double-digit B&M UK margin (UK was 12.2% in FY25), with France scaling and Heron stabilised; still about 0.4pp below the FY23-25 group average.
bull.terminal_cap_note: Exit-multiple cap tested and not binding. On the like-for-like IFRS 16 basis the Gordon terminal value is 7.4x EBITDA against a 10-year maximum of 8.89x; the existing 15x FCF cap is tighter than the historical-multiple cap (18.4x FCF equivalent) and is kept.

bear.ebitda_margin_note: Year 1 at the bottom of FY27 guidance (GBP 450m) less adjusting items; then a further 0.5pp of erosion as price investment and wage inflation outrun LFL.
bear.terminal_cap_note: Exit-multiple cap from the sanity-check fix (2026-11-19): bear terminal value limited to the 10-year minimum EV/EBITDA of 5.68x. That history is on the IFRS 16 basis (statutory EBITDA before rent, debt including lease liabilities), so it is converted to this model's pre-IFRS 16 basis: FY2036 EBITDA 492.7 + rent add-back at the FY26 ratio of 4.78% of revenue (336.5) = 829.2; x 5.68 = 4,710 lease-inclusive EV; less lease liabilities at the FY26 ratio of 25.2% of revenue (1,773) = 2,937, which is 11.6x terminal FCF. The engine applies min(Gordon, cap x FCF), and the cap binds (Gordon was 14.6x FCF).

scenario_narratives.base: Back to B&M Basics works partially. UK like-for-likes settle at low single digits, General Merchandise category margin is rebuilt but FMCG price investment against Home Bargains is permanent, and the FY26 statutory cost step-up (minimum wage, employer NI, EPR levy) is never recovered. Group pre-IFRS 16 EBITDA margin climbs from the FY27 guidance midpoint (c.7.8% after adjusting items) to 9.5% by FY32, a little under half-way back to the 11.1-11.5% of FY23-25. UK openings return to 25-35 gross a year from FY28 and France adds 15-20, giving c.4% revenue growth fading to 2.5%.
scenario_narratives.bull: The turnaround succeeds in full: sustained UK LFL of 3%+ across FMCG and General Merchandise, the B&M 2.0 refit lifts productivity of the existing estate, Ellesmere Port automation lowers cost per case, France reaches scale at double-digit margins and Heron returns to growth under new management. B&M UK regains the low-double-digit margin management targets and the group reaches 11.0%, with revenue growth of c.5% from both LFL and a faster rollout toward 1,200 UK stores.
scenario_narratives.bear: The H1 FY27 improvement proves to be a price-funded bounce. Home Bargains and the grocers keep taking share, LFL slips back to flat, and wage, freight and energy inflation outrun pricing power, so the group margin drifts from the bottom of FY27 guidance down to 7.0%. The rollout is slowed to protect the 1.0-1.5x leverage range, Heron keeps shrinking, and growth runs at c.2%. The business remains comfortably cash-generative and solvent in this case; the downside is a permanently lower-margin retailer, not distress.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: the thesis rests on a turnaround only about a year old, run by a new CEO with a permanent CFO not starting until January 2027, against a privately-held competitor that is currently out-executing B&M. Base 50%: guidance has just been introduced with H1 EBITDA up 6% and positive early Golden Quarter trading, which supports stabilisation but not yet a margin rebuild. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs UK LFL, category margin, France and Heron all to work together and management frames its margin target as a medium-term outcome without a date.

valuation_philosophy.summary: B&M is valued as a cash-generative discount retailer in the early stage of a turnaround, on unlevered owner free cash flow after rent. Year 1 is the FY27 guidance midpoint, neither the FY26 trough nor the pre-FY26 peak, and the base case recovers just under half of the lost margin (7.0% / 9.5% / 11.0% mature EBITDA margin in bear / base / bull). SANITY CHECK: the multiples check tripped on one rule, an implied P/E of 25.0x against a 10-year average of 12.1x. The denominator is FY26 statutory EPS, which halved in the trough year; on FY26 adjusted EPS or FY27 guidance the same value is about 17x, and on base-case FY30 earnings about 12x. The market price itself already sits at roughly 23x trough EPS, within 7% of the trip threshold, so the rule fires on almost any value modestly above the current quote. WHAT CHANGED: the terminal values were tested against the historical EV/EBITDA range (bear = 10-year minimum 5.68x, base = average 7.59x, bull = maximum 8.89x), after converting the model's pre-IFRS 16 EBITDA to the lease-inclusive basis the history is measured on. Base (7.1x) and bull (7.4x) were already below their caps and are unchanged. The bear terminal was at 6.6x and has been cut to the 5.68x minimum, which lowers the bear value from 240p to about 208p and the weighted value from 391p to about 383p. The previously reported '14.6x exit multiple' is terminal value over free cash flow, not EV/EBITDA; the like-for-like EV/EBITDA exit was never above the historical average. WACC stays at 9.0%: mid-cycle rebasing was already in the first build and no structural premium applies. RESULT: the check grades the base-case value (400p), which the like-for-like cap leaves unchanged, so the rule still trips: 25.0x trough P/E against a 24.2x limit (base value about 3% over it), 5.0x book (average 5.0x), 9.2x trailing EV/EBITDA on trough EBITDA (average 7.6x, maximum 8.9x) and 0.70x sales (average 0.90x). The fix shows up in the weighted value instead (391p to 383p). The residual P/E trip is accepted as a trough-denominator artefact and has not been tuned away; applying the historical multiple to the model's after-rent EBITDA without the lease conversion would have forced a pass (base about 385p) by mixing two accounting bases. FRAMING: this is a turnaround-recovery valuation, not a bargain. The value is within single digits of the market price, the shares have already re-rated sharply on the first evidence of stabilisation, and a value-trap outcome (the bear case, 25% weight, a permanently 7%-margin retailer) is worth a little over half the current price. An owner is paid only if the margin rebuild goes beyond what the base case assumes; there is no margin of safety at this price.
key_risks_to_valuation: Trailing earnings do not support the value: it rests on a margin recovery from 7.9% toward 9.5% that has one half-year of evidence behind it
Mature group EBITDA margin: each 1pp is worth very roughly 15% of base equity value
Reported adjusted EBITDA excludes adjusting items that recur most years (GBP 60m in FY26); the model allows only 0.1-0.2pp for them
FY26 and H1 FY27 cash flow was helped by working-capital inflows that management expects to stabilise, not repeat
The share price rose about 30% in the two weeks before the valuation date on the H1 results, so much of the recovery now in the base case is already in the price
Lease commitments of GBP 1.45bn sit outside net debt under the chosen treatment; they are paid for through the pre-IFRS 16 margin, and store closures in a bear case would not shed them quickly

Base and bull exit caps tested, not binding
Anchors, driver paths, WACC, weights: unchanged

reconciliation.unchanged: Everything except the bear terminal cap is deliberately unchanged: price and balance-sheet anchors (same day), all growth, margin, capex, tax and working-capital paths, WACC 9.0%, terminal growth 2.0%, weights 25/50/25. Evidence that would move them: Golden Quarter trading (January 2027 update) for year-1 margin; FY27 results for the adjusting-items allowance and working capital; two consecutive halves of UK LFL above 3% with stable gross margin for the base mature margin.
